meaning: Energy input from laser/electron/arc source. Too low may cause lack of fusion; too high may cause keyhole/evaporation.
Beam travel speed. Higher speed usually lowers line energy and can increase lack-of-fusion risk.
Distance between adjacent scan tracks. Large hatch spacing can leave un-melted regions.
Powder/deposition layer height. Thicker layers need higher energy for full melting.
Approximate beam spot size. Used for power density and melt-pool stability proxies.
Measured density relative to theoretical density. A major property driver, especially fatigue/elongation.
Void fraction. Higher porosity usually reduces ductility and fatigue performance.
Average grain size from OM/SEM/EBSD/TEM where reported.
Qualitative structure: equiaxed, columnar, cellular, dendritic, martensitic, mixed.
Texture strength from EBSD/XRD, multiple of random distribution.
Main phase: austenite, alpha/beta, gamma, alpha-Al, Cu, martensite, etc.
Precipitates or intermetallics: Laves, gamma prime, carbides, Si network, alpha prime, etc.
